source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.attribution: Generalized forward-only conditional support-growth consequence of Definition4.1 and Lemma4.2 forward (printed34–35/PDF46–47). Not the full source iff or a support-existence theorem.

source_delta: Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization, arXiv:1912.13213v10. Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 forward, printed 34–35 / PDF 46–47. The printed lemma is an equivalence with a subgradient-domain condition throughout V. This library statement keeps only the forward implication at one supplied support, restricted to V, and generalizes the finite-dimensional vector pairing to a continuous real covector on an arbitrary normed space. Continuity is stronger than algebraic necessity. No inner-product norm is imposed. The affine-tilt implementation below is distinct from the source segment-and-limit proof.
exact_header:
theorem stronglyConvex_support_growth {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (f : E → EReal) (V : Set E) (lam : ℝ)
    (hf : SourceProper f) (hV : Convex ℝ V)
    (hdom : V ⊆ effectiveDomain f) (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (hstrong : ∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → a < 1 →
      f (a • x + (1 - a) • y) ≤
        (a : EReal) * f x + ((1 - a : ℝ) : EReal) * f y -
          (((lam / 2) * a * (1 - a) * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal))
    (p : E) (hp : p ∈ V) (g : E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (hsupport : ∀ z ∈ V, f p + (g (z - p) : EReal) ≤ f z)
    (q : E) (hq : q ∈ V) :
    (f p).toReal + g (q - p) + (lam / 2) * ‖q - p‖ ^ 2 ≤ (f q).toReal
supplied_premises: Proper extended-real f, convex literal V contained in effectiveDomain f, λ≥0, exact strong interpolation
p∈V, q∈V, supplied continuous linear functional g
Explicit local support hsupport: for every z∈V, f(p)+g(z−p)≤f(z)
not_produced: Support existence at p or other V points
Attainment/coercivity/compactness or constrained cumulative objective hypotheses
Theorem6.9 support witness or full corrected regret bounds
native_proof: Define the extended-real function F(x) = f(x) − g(x − p), including outside V. The subtracted term is always real. Since f never equals negative infinity, neither does F; the feasible point p supplies a finite witness. Thus F is proper and finite on V. For a feasible segment, linearity gives g(a x + (1 − a)y − p) = a g(x − p) + (1 − a)g(y − p). Subtracting this identity from the strong interpolation inequality preserves the same λ/2 penalty, so F satisfies the same strong-convexity hypothesis. The supplied support gives F(p) ≤ F(z) for every z ∈ V, using g(0) = 0. This proves a minimum of the tilt internally; no minimum premise is added. Apply stronglyConvex_minimum_growth to F and simplify its finite endpoint values to recover the quadratic support bound for f.
boundary: This is a generalized forward implication at a supplied local support, not the full equivalence in Lemma 4.2. It does not establish support existence, a global source subgradient, vector-to-covector transport, or attainment for a cumulative objective. The source-support obligation in Theorem 6.9 and corrected full regret bounds remain separate. Chapter 2 and the book remain incomplete.
